_comment: Field battles: an army holding a hex fights any horde whose route crosses it. Ambush: on `ambush.terrain`, with the army in place `ambush.prepMinutes` game minutes before the horde arrives, the defenders' first round hits `ambush.bonus` harder and the horde fights it without its stance. Choke point: a passable hex with at least `choke.minBlockedNeighbors` impassable neighbours; attackers hit `choke.attackerFactor` as hard there, and Hold the Line gains `choke.holdTheLineDefense` defense. River: a horde that crossed a river into the hex it fights in (over a bridge; nothing crosses elsewhere) hits `river.attackerFactor` as hard, at walls or in the field. Forts are built within `fort.range` hexes of a village and give armies holding them `fort.defenseBonus` defense and `fort.attackBonus` attack (and ease their maneuvers, battle.json lines.fort); a fort an army holds has a zone of control: no horde steps onto a hex beside it without attacking it, so a horde keeps two hexes away from it, unless that way round costs more than `fort.zoneDetour` more than the straight road, when it marches on the fort first and on to its target after; each keeps up to `fort.grainCapacity` grain. Supply points are built like forts (within `supplyPoint.range` hexes, paid from the village, standing after `supplyPoint.buildSeconds`) and keep up to `supplyPoint.grainCapacity` grain, but give no defense. An army that arrives at or stands on a fort or supply point fills up from its grain as it would in a village, and a standing army can leave grain there from its own supply. A horde that passes within its raid reach of a supply point (built or being built) burns it, grain and all, unless an army stands on it; forts keep their grain behind their walls. Bridges are built over a river edge within `bridge.range` hexes of a village (game seconds, divided by world speed); until one stands nothing crosses there, hordes included. Roads are built between two neighbouring hexes within `road.range` of a village, (a road into impassable land with a `roadMoveCost`, a mountain pass, costs `mountainFactor` times as much and takes `mountainFactor` times as long, every level), and improved twice more: each of `road.levels` is paid from the village and done after its `buildSeconds`, and moving along a road costs its level's `factor` of the terrain (a road being improved keeps its level until the work is done), for players and the human hordes alike, but the Monsters of the North keep off them. A fire that reaches a hex damages every road into it (`damage`): a damaged road saves only `effect` of what it would save of the march (a road of factor f costs 1 - (1 - f) x effect of the terrain) and adds only `effect` of its outpostBonus, until a village in range repairs it, for `repairShare` of its level's cost and build time (a mountain pass's included); a damaged road can't be improved until it is repaired, and a fire reaching a road under repair undoes the work. An outpost joined to its village by roads gathers more: over the fewest road steps between them (of those, the best built), the average of each step's level `outpostBonus` is added to its yield. Terraforming (`terraform`): a village reshapes the land within `range` hexes of it, on a hex with no village, outpost, fort, camp or site and no other work under way there: each of `actions` turns the terrain named in `from` into the one it maps to, is paid at once (`cost`, mostly grain to feed the workers) and done after `hours` game hours (divided by world speed); clearing a forest also brings its timber, levelling hills their stone (`gain`), to the village. A work with `river` digs a river along the edge between its hex and a neighbouring one (both land, not yet a river there, and corner to corner with a river already there): when it is done nothing crosses that edge without a bridge. Neither a river nor a lake may be made where it would cut a village off from the Holy City. Whatever is already on the road when the work is done keeps its road; roads planned after go round. A work with `fire` sets the forest alight (never where an army stands): while it burns (its `hours`) nothing can enter the hex, armies, caravans, scouts and hordes alike, and hordes, armies, caravans and settlers already on a road into it while it burns plan their way again from where they are: round it, or waiting at its edge until it is out, whichever arrives sooner; with `spreadChance` the fire spreads to each neighbouring hex it could burn (the land in `from`, but never a settlement or a hex an army stands on, which stop it) `spreadHours` later, at most `generations` hexes from where it was set, burning any outpost (to ruins), fort, supply point or camp there; a burnt hex becomes what `from` names, and its timber is lost. Wagon fort: an army holding open ground (no fort, supply point or village) with wagons (units.json `wagon`) can draw them into a ring, ready after `wagonFort.setupMinutes` game minutes; it gives `wagonFort.bonusPerWagon` defense for each wagon per `wagonFort.menPerWagon` soldiers (wagons x bonusPerWagon / ceil(soldiers / menPerWagon)), at most `wagonFort.maxBonus`, and breaks up when the army moves.

clear.name: Clear the forest
clear.description: Fell the trees for the land beneath: forest becomes plains, wooded hills bare hills, and the timber comes home.

plant.name: Plant trees
plant.description: Sow a wood: plains become forest, hills wooded hills, for woodcutters and outposts to come. Nothing comes home.

drain.name: Drain the swamp
drain.description: Dig ditches until the swamp is dry plains. Nothing comes home.

level.name: Level the hills
level.description: Cut the hills down to plains; the stone comes home.

burn.name: Burn the forest
burn.description: Set the forest alight: nothing gets through while it burns, and the fire may spread to the trees around it, burning what stands there. Forest becomes plains, wooded hills bare hills; the timber is lost.

flood.name: Make a lake
flood.description: Dam the streams until the plains or the swamp lie under water: a lake for fishermen and boats, and a wall no army crosses.

soak.name: Make a wetland
soak.description: Turn the streams onto the plains until they are swamp: slow, treacherous ground for any horde.

river.name: Extend a river
river.description: Dig the river on along this hex's edge, toward the hex you choose: nothing crosses it without a bridge.
